title: Material Energy Conservation Studio
description: A material experimentation studio where a glass vase with flowers, a skull, and a carbon fibre object sit on pedestals. The user redistributes a fixed budget of material energy across all three objects, adjusting roughness, metalness, transmission, and emissive intensity while a conservation law ensures total energy remains constant. Multi-input sliders are coupled so boosting one property on one object automatically reduces available energy elsewhere, with full undo/redo support.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a Material Energy Conservation Studio. Load three GLB assets: GlassVaseFlowers.glb on the left pedestal, ScatteringSkull.glb in the center, and CarbonFibre.glb on the right. Use GLTFLoader from CDN. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 6) looking at origin. Add an HDR-style environment using PMREMGenerator with a simple procedural sky or a neutral studio environment for reflections. Include one DirectionalLight and one AmbientLight. Enable OrbitControls for camera rotation. Create three cylindrical pedestal meshes beneath each model. Implement a fixed Material Energy Budget of 4.0 units total shared across all three objects. Build a left-side HTML panel with three collapsible sections, one per object. Each section has four sliders: roughness (0-1), metalness (0-1), transmission (0-1), and emissive intensity (0-1). Each slider value contributes to total energy consumption. Enforce a conservation law: the sum of all 12 slider values must not exceed 4.0. When a user increases one slider, if the budget would be exceeded, proportionally scale down all other sliders across all objects to maintain the cap, visually updating their positions. Clicking an object highlights it with an outline effect or glow and scrolls the panel to its section. Display a real-time energy bar at the top showing used vs remaining budget with color gradient from green to red. Implement an undo/redo stack supporting at least 20 states. Add undo (Ctrl+Z) and redo (Ctrl+Shift+Z) keyboard shortcuts plus two buttons in the UI. Each slider change pushes a snapshot of all 12 values onto the stack. Apply material changes in real-time by traversing each loaded model's meshes and updating their MeshPhysicalMaterial properties. Add a Reset button that restores all sliders to default values (roughness 0.5, metalness 0.0, transmission 0.0, emissive 0.0) and clears the undo stack. Animate a subtle rotation on each pedestal. The interaction requires approximately 12 steps: select each object, adjust multiple coupled sliders observing conservation redistribution, undo several changes, redo them, and reset.
